title.sourceEnglish: The Three Ethics: Earth Care, People Care, Fair Share
title.tshivendaDraft: Milayo Miraru ya Vhuḓifari: U Ṱhogomela Mavu na Mupo, U Ṱhogomela Vhathu, U Kovhelana ho Fanelaho

body.sourceEnglish:
Permaculture rests on three ethics. Earth Care means treating soil, water, plants and animals as living systems to protect, not resources to use up. People Care means your family's needs come first, then your community's. Fair Share means taking only what you need and returning the surplus — seeds, food, water, knowledge — back into the system.

These aren't abstract ideas. A farmer who sells every egg and vegetable but keeps nothing back for the family table is skipping People Care. A community that fences off a shared spring is breaking Fair Share.

Ethics matter because they help you decide when there's no rulebook — a neighbour asking to graze cattle after a drought, a flood damaging your swales. Build these three into how you think before you build anything on the ground.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Permaculture yo thewa kha milayo miraru ya vhuḓifari. U Ṱhogomela Mavu na Mupo (Earth Care) zwi amba u dzhia mavu, maḓi, zwimela na zwipuka sa maitele a no tshila a fanelaho u tsireledzwa, hu si zwiko zwine zwa fanela u fhedzwa. U Ṱhogomela Vhathu (People Care) zwi amba uri ṱhoḓea dza muṱa waṋu dzi dzia u ranga, ha kona u tevhela dza tshitshavha tsha haṋu. U Kovhelana ho Fanelaho (Fair Share) zwi amba u dzhia fhedzi zwine na zwi ṱoḓa nahone na vhuedzedza zwo salaho (surplus) — mbeu, zwiḽiwa, maḓi, nḓivho — murahu kha maitele.

Hezwi a si mihumbulo fhedzi i sa vhonali. Mulimi ane a rengisa makumba oṱhe na miroho yoṱhe fhedzi a si siele ṱafula ḽa muṱa tshithu u khou pfuka u Ṱhogomela Vhathu. Tshitshavha tshine tsha thivhela tshisima tshi kovhelanwaho nga lufhenḓe tshi khou pwanya u Kovhelana ho Fanelaho.

Milayo ya vhuḓifari ndi ya ndeme ngauri i ni thusa u dzhia tsheo musi hu si na bugu ya milayo — muhura ane a khou humbela u fulisa kholomo nga murahu ha gomelelo, mandindi ane a khou tshinyadza dzi-swale dzaṋu. Fhaṱani hezwi zwiraru kha nḓila ine na humbula ngayo musi ni sa athu fhaṱa tshithu fhasi.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Earth Care: protect soil, water, and biodiversity
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: U Ṱhogomela Mavu na Mupo: tsireledzani mavu, maḓi, na u fhambana ha zwitshili (biodiversity)

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: People Care: your family's needs come before market production
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: U Ṱhogomela Vhathu: ṱhoḓea dza muṱa waṋu dzi ranga zwi no bviselwa makete

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Fair Share: return surplus to the system — seeds, water, food, knowledge
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: U Kovhelana ho Fanelaho: vhuedzedzani zwo salaho kha maitele — mbeu, maḓi, zwiḽiwa, nḓivho

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Ethics guide decisions when there's no rulebook
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Milayo ya vhuḓifari i livhisa tsheo musi hu si na bugu ya milayo

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer sells all his surplus maize but keeps nothing for composting or seed saving. Which ethic is he most failing?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi u rengisa mavhele (maize) oṱhe o salaho fhedzi a si vhulunge tshithu u itela u ita khomposo (composting) kana u vhulunga mbeu. Ndi ufhio mulayo wa vhuḓifari une a khou u kundelwa zwihulwane?

options.sourceEnglish: Earth Care only
options.tshivendaDraft: U Ṱhogomela Mavu na Mupo fhedzi

options.sourceEnglish: People Care only
options.tshivendaDraft: U Ṱhogomela Vhathu fhedzi

options.sourceEnglish: Fair Share — he returns nothing to the system
options.tshivendaDraft: U Kovhelana ho Fanelaho — ha humiseli tshithu kha maitele

options.sourceEnglish: All three equally
options.tshivendaDraft: Zwoṱhe zwiraru nga u lingana

rationale.sourceEnglish: Fair Share means returning some of what you take — as seed, compost, or food for others. Selling everything and keeping nothing back breaks that cycle.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: U Kovhelana ho Fanelaho zwi amba u vhuedzedza tshiṅwe tsha zwine na dzhia — sa mbeu, khomposo, kana zwiḽiwa zwa vhaṅwe. U rengisa zwoṱhe na u sa vhulunga tshithu murahu zwi pwanya wonoyo mudzinginyo.

question.sourceEnglish: Your borehole serves your household. Neighbours ask for water too. Which action best reflects all three ethics?
question.tshivendaDraft: Tshisima tshaṋu tsha borehole tshi shumela muṱa waṋu. Vhahura vha khou humbela maḓi-vho. Ndi tshifhio tshiito tshine tsha sumbedza zwavhuḓi milayo yoṱhe miraru ya vhuḓifari?

options.sourceEnglish: Sell access to the highest bidder
options.tshivendaDraft: Rengisani thendelo ya u shumisa kha ane a khou badela tshelede nnzhi tshoṱhe

options.sourceEnglish: Keep all the borehole water for a larger irrigation area
options.tshivendaDraft: Vhulungani maḓi oṱhe a borehole u itela fhethu huhulwane ha u sheledza

options.sourceEnglish: Find out if sharing is allowed and if the borehole can serve all users. Only then agree how to share fairly and keep watching the water level.
options.tshivendaDraft: Wanani uri naa u kovhelana ho tendelwa na uri borehole i nga kona u shumela vhashumisi vhoṱhe. Ndi hone fhedzi ni tshi tendelana nga ha nḓila ya u kovhelana nga nḓila yo teaho nahone ni bvele phanḓa u sedza vhuimo ha maḓi.

options.sourceEnglish: Cap the borehole to preserve groundwater only
options.tshivendaDraft: Tibani borehole u itela u tsireledza maḓi a re nga fhasi ha mavu fhedzi

rationale.sourceEnglish: First find out what water use is allowed and whether the source can serve all users without taking too much. If sharing is allowed and there is enough water, agree how to share fairly. Monitoring helps you notice change; it does not give permission to take more water.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: U ranga u wana uri ndi kushumisele-ḓe kwa maḓi kwo tendelwaho na uri naa tshiko tshi nga kona u shumela vhashumisi vhoṱhe hu si na u dzhia zwinzhi lwo kalaho. Arali u kovhelana ho tendelwa nahone maḓi e o eḓana, tendelanani nga ha nḓila ya u kovhelana nga nḓila yo teaho. U sedza zwi ni thusa u vhona tshanduko; a zwi ṋei thendelo ya u dzhia maḓi manzhi.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Twelve design principles arranged as segments around a central seedling, each shown as a simple picture — an eye for observing, a droplet for catching water, a sun for energy, a loop for returning waste.
infographicAlt.tshivendaDraft: Maitele a fumi na mavhili a mufhaṱo o vhekanywaho sa zwipiḓa u monymona na tshimela tshiṱuku tsha vhukati, tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tsho sumbedzwa sa tshifanyiso tsho leluwaho — iṱo ḽa u sedza, ḓoḓi ḽa u fara maḓi, ḓuvha ḽa maanḓa, na mudzinginyo wa u vhuedzedza mitshelo na malaṱwa.

title.tshivendaDraft: Maitele a Fumi na Mavhili: U Ita design na Mupo

body.sourceEnglish:
David Holmgren set out twelve design principles in Essence of Permaculture. Bill Mollison and David Holmgren co-originated the permaculture concept. Three useful starting points for this lesson are: observe and interact — watch your land through a full season before major earthworks; catch and store energy — notice rain, sun and biomass before they leave your property; and use edges and value the marginal — a fence line or strip beside a path can be a useful place to observe.

Others worth knowing: produce no waste (scraps become compost, compost becomes soil), use small and slow solutions (a bucket can irrigate a bed without electricity), and use and value diversity. Hail injury to maize depends on the storm and the crop’s growth stage.

Pick two or three principles that speak to your biggest problem and apply them hard. The rest become obvious as you go.
body.tshivendaDraft:
David Holmgren o vhea maitele a design a fumi na mavhili kha Essence of Permaculture. Bill Mollison na David Holmgren vho thoma muhumbulo wa permaculture vhoṱhe. Maitele mararu a vhuedzaho u thoma ngao kha hei ngudo ndi haya: observe and interact — sedzani land yaṋu kha khalaṅwaha yoṱhe ni sa athu ita major earthworks; catch and store energy — ṱhogomelani mvula, ḓuvha na biomass zwi sa athu bva kha ndaka yaṋu; na use edges and value the marginal — muduba wa fence kana tshipiḓa tshi re tsini na nḓila (strip) tshi nga vha fhethu hu vhuedzaho ha u sedza.

Maṅwe maitele ane zwa vhuedza u a ḓivha ndi haya: produce no waste (masalela a vha compost, compost ya vha mavu); use small and slow solutions (bakete ḽi nga sheledza planting bed hu si na muḓagasi); na use and value diversity. Hail injury kha maize i ya nga storm na growth stage ya crop.

Khethani maitele mavhili kana mararu ane a tshimbidzana na thaidzo yaṋu khulwanesa, nahone ni a shumise nga mafulufulu. Maṅwe a ḓo tou vha khagala musi ni tshi khou bvela phanḓa.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Observe your land for a full season before major earthworks
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Sedzani land yaṋu kha khalaṅwaha yoṱhe ni sa athu ita major earthworks

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Catch and store rain, sun, and biomass before they leave your property
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Farani nahone ni vhulunge mvula, ḓuvha na biomass zwi sa athu bva kha ndaka yaṋu

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Edges and margins can be useful places to observe what grows well
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Edges na margins zwi nga vha fhethu hu vhuedzaho ha u sedza zwine zwa aluwa zwavhuḓi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Hail injury to maize depends on the storm and the crop’s growth stage
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Hail injury kha maize i ya nga storm na growth stage ya crop

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to dig swales to harvest rainwater. What should she do first, following 'observe and interact'?
question.tshivendaDraft: Mulimi u ṱoḓa u bwa swales u itela u kuvhanganya maḓi a mvula. Ndi mini zwine a fanela u ranga u zwi ita a tshi tevhedza observe and interact?

options.sourceEnglish: Dig immediately after the first good rain
options.tshivendaDraft: Bwani nga u ṱavhanya nga murahu ha mvula ya u ranga yavhuḓi

options.sourceEnglish: Watch where water flows and pools across at least one wet season
options.tshivendaDraft: Sedzani hune maḓi a elela hone na hune a kuvhangana hone kha at least one wet season

options.sourceEnglish: Copy a neighbour's swale layout
options.tshivendaDraft: Kopisani kuitele kwa swale ya muhura

options.sourceEnglish: Assume the same swale design fits every site
options.tshivendaDraft: Humbulani uri design nthihi ya swale i lingana na site iṅwe na iṅwe

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet season shows more than one storm, but observation is only a first step. Check the soil, slope, drainage and safe overflow route with a trained local adviser before digging.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Khalaṅwaha ya mvula i sumbedza madumbu a no fhira ḽithihi, fhedzi u sedza ndi vhukando ha u ranga fhedzi. Musi ni sa athu bwa, na mueletshedzi wa henefho o gudedzwaho, tolani mavu, slope, drainage na safe overflow route.

question.sourceEnglish: Which layout best applies 'integrate rather than segregate'?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ndi layout ifhio ine ya shumisa zwavhuḓi integrate rather than segregate?

options.sourceEnglish: Chickens penned far from the garden
options.tshivendaDraft: Khuhu dzo valelwaho kule na tsimu

options.sourceEnglish: Garden, fruit trees and a chicken run arranged so chickens use an empty bed after harvest, then the farmer checks safe management before edible crops return
options.tshivendaDraft: Tsimu, miri ya mitshelo na chicken run zwo vhekanywa nga nḓila ine khuhu dza shumisa planting bed i si na zwimela nga murahu ha harvest; nga murahu mulimi u tola safe management musi edible crops dzi sa athu vhuya

options.sourceEnglish: Separate paddocks for each crop
options.tshivendaDraft: Paddocks dzo fhambanaho dza crop iṅwe na iṅwe

options.sourceEnglish: All animals kept off the cultivated zone
options.tshivendaDraft: Zwifuwo zwoṱhe zwi dzule nnḓa ha cultivated zone

rationale.sourceEnglish: Integration puts each element to work for its neighbours — here, chickens clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen. Fresh manure can carry germs, so check safe management before edible crops return.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Integration i ita uri element iṅwe na iṅwe i shumele zwine zwa vha tsini nayo — hafha, khuhu dzi clean up pests na u engedza fertility, nṱhani ha u dzula dzi sa shumi kha fixed pen. Fresh manure i nga hwalela germs, ngauralo tola safe management musi edible crops dzi sa athu vhuya.

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Illustrated example farm: numbered markers 0 to 5 follow a winding footpath from the house and near garden, past chickens and a field, toward trees and a wilder riverside area. The markers are examples, not fixed boundaries or distances.

title.sourceEnglish: Zones and Sectors: Organising Your Farm by Energy
title.tshivendaDraft: Zoune na Sekithara: U Dzudzanya Bulasi Yaṋu nga Maanḓa

body.sourceEnglish:
Zones and sectors help you cut wasted labour. Zones run 0 to 5 by how often you visit. Zone 0 is the house. In this example, Zone 1 is near the house and holds what you pick often — herbs, salad greens. Zone 2 is the main garden and chicken run, visited once or twice a day. Zone 3 is the main field, visited weekly. Zone 4 is semi-wild — fruit trees and fodder needing occasional attention. Zone 5 is left wild.

Sectors are the energies arriving from outside — sun, wind, rain, flood, fire. Watch where strong wind comes from on your farm. Nearby weather-station records can help you check wind direction. Watch where rainwater enters and flows across your land. Draw arrows for what you observe.

Sketch zones and sectors on paper and you have the skeleton of your design.
body.tshivendaDraft:
Zones na sectors zwi thusa u fhungudza mushumo u sa ṱoḓei. Zones dzi bva kha 0 u ya kha 5, zwi tshi tevhedza uri ni dalela fhethu honoho lunzhi-lini. Zone 0 ndi nnḓu. Kha tsumbo iyi, Zone 1 i tsini na nnḓu nahone i na zwine na zwi ka lunzhi — herbs na muroho wa saladi. Zone 2 ndi serapa tshihulwane na chicken run, zwine zwa dalelwa luthihi kana luvhili nga ḓuvha. Zone 3 ndi tsimu khulwane, ine ya dalelwa vhege iṅwe na iṅwe. Zone 4 ndi semi-wild — miri ya mitshelo na fodder zwine zwa ṱoḓa ṱhogomelo nga zwiṅwe zwifhinga. Zone 5 yo siwa i wild.

Sectors ndi energy dzi no swika dzi tshi bva nnḓa — ḓuvha, muya, mvula, mandindi na mulilo. Sedzani hune muya u re na maanḓa wa bva hone bulasini yaṋu. Rekhodo dza weather station ya tsini dzi nga thusa u sedza thungo ya muya. Sedzani hune maḓi a mvula a dzhena hone na hune a elela hone kha land yaṋu. Olani misevhe u sumbedza zwe na zwi vhona.

Olani zones na sectors kha bammbiri, nahone ni vha ni na motheo wa pulane yaṋu.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: In this example, Zone 1 near the house holds often-picked herbs
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Kha tsumbo iyi, Zone 1 i re tsini na nnḓu i na herbs dzine na dzi ka lunzhi.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Zones organise labour by how often you need to visit
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Zoune dzi dzudzanya mishumo nga nḓila ine na fanela u dalela ngayo

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Sectors map incoming sun, wind, rainwater, flood and fire
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Sekithara dzi ita mmapa wa ḓuvha ḽi no ḓa, muya, maḓi a mvula, mandindi na mulilo

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A simple sketch of zones and sectors is enough to start designing
keyPoints.tshivendaDraft: Nyolo yo leluwaho ya zones na sectors yo lingana u thoma design.

question.sourceEnglish: You plant herbs in Zone 3, the main field far from the house. What problem does this create?
question.tshivendaDraft: Ni ṱavha herbs kha Zone 3, tsimu khulwane i re kule na nnḓu. Hezwi zwi vhanga thaidzo-ḓe?

options.sourceEnglish: Herbs grow too large
options.tshivendaDraft: Herbs dzi aluwa zwihulwane lwo kalaho

options.sourceEnglish: The extra walk may mean you pick or check them less often
options.tshivendaDraft: Lwendo lwo engedzeaho lu nga amba uri ni nga ka kana u sedza herbs less often

options.sourceEnglish: Herbs cross-pollinate with main crops
options.tshivendaDraft: Herbs dzi cross-pollinate na zwimela zwihulwane

options.sourceEnglish: Zone 3 gets too much sun for herbs
options.tshivendaDraft: Zone 3 i wana ḓuvha ḽinzhi lwo kalaho kha herbs

rationale.sourceEnglish: Put a crop you pick often near a daily path. A distant bed adds walking and may be checked less often.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Vheani tshimela tshine na tshi ka lunzhi tsini ha nḓila ya ḓuvha ḽiṅwe na ḽiṅwe. Bed i re kule i engedza u tshimbila nahone i nga tolwa less often.

question.sourceEnglish: You observe damaging wind coming from the north-west on a Highveld farm. Where should a windbreak go?
question.tshivendaDraft: Musi ni tshi vhona “damaging wind coming from the north-west on a Highveld farm”, windbreak i fanela u vhewa ngafhi?

options.sourceEnglish: South-east boundary
options.tshivendaDraft: Moedi wa South-east

options.sourceEnglish: North-west boundary, between the wind and the crops
options.tshivendaDraft: Moedi wa North-west, vhukati ha muya na zwimela

options.sourceEnglish: Centre of the property
options.tshivendaDraft: Vhukati ha land yaṋu

options.sourceEnglish: Windbreaks aren't needed since winds are seasonal
options.tshivendaDraft: Windbreaks a dzi ṱoḓei ngauri mimuya i ya nga khalaṅwaha

rationale.sourceEnglish: A windbreak works by standing between the wind source and what it would damage — so it belongs on the side the wind actually comes from.
rationale.tshivendaDraft: Windbreak i shuma nga u ima vhukati ha hune muya wa bva hone na tshine ya nga tshi tshinya — ngauralo i fanela u vha kha sia ḽine muya wa bva khaḽo zwa vhukuma.

title.sourceEnglish: The Three Ethics: Earth Care, People Care, Fair Share
title.xitsongaDraft: Mahanyelo Manharhu: Ku Hlayisa Misava, Ku Hlayisa Vanhu, Ku Avelana hi Ku Ringana

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: The three ethics as three linked circles of equal size: a hand holding soil for Earth Care, two people for People Care, and a basket passing between hands for Fair Share.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Mahanyelo lawa manharhu ma kombisiwa hi swirhendzevutana swinharhu leswi hlanganisiweke, leswi ringanaka hi vukulu: voko leri khomeke misava ra Ku Hlayisa Misava; vanhu vambirhi va Ku Hlayisa Vanhu; na baskiti leri hundziseriwaka hi mavoko ra Ku Avelana hi Ku Ringana.

body.sourceEnglish:
Permaculture rests on three ethics. Earth Care means treating soil, water, plants and animals as living systems to protect, not resources to use up. People Care means your family's needs come first, then your community's. Fair Share means taking only what you need and returning the surplus — seeds, food, water, knowledge — back into the system.

These aren't abstract ideas. A farmer who sells every egg and vegetable but keeps nothing back for the family table is skipping People Care. A community that fences off a shared spring is breaking Fair Share.

Ethics matter because they help you decide when there's no rulebook — a neighbour asking to graze cattle after a drought, a flood damaging your swales. Build these three into how you think before you build anything on the ground.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Permaculture yi seketeriwe eka mahanyelo manharhu. Ku Hlayisa Misava swi vula ku teka misava, mati, swimilana na swiharhi tanihi maendlelo lama hanyaka lama faneleke ku sirheleriwa, ku nga ri switirhisiwa swo hela hi ku tirhisiwa. Ku Hlayisa Vanhu swi vula leswaku swilaveko swa ndyangu wa wena swi rhanga emahlweni, kutani ku landzela swa vaaki va ka n'wina. Ku Avelana hi Ku Ringana swi vula ku teka ntsena leswi u swi lavaka kutani u vuyisela leswi saleke — mbewu, swakudya, mati, vutivi — endzeni ka maendlelo ya nsimu.

Lawa a hi mianakanyo ntsena leyi nga riki ya xiviri. Murimi loyi a xavisaka matandza hinkwawo na matsavu kambe a nga siyi nchumu etafuleni ra ndyangu u tlula Ku Hlayisa Vanhu. Vaaki lava biyelaka xihlovo lexi avelaneriwaka va tlula Ku Avelana hi Ku Ringana.

Mahanyelo i ya nkoka hikuva ma ku pfuna ku endla swiboho loko ku nga ri na buku ya milawu — muakelani loyi a kombelaka ku risa tihomu endzhaku ka dyandza, kumbe ndhambi leyi onhaka swisele (swales) swa wena. Aka mahanyelo lawa manharhu eka ndlela leyi u anakanyaka ha yona u nga si aka nchumu emisaveni.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Earth Care: protect soil, water, and biodiversity
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Ku Hlayisa Misava: sirelela misava, mati na ku hambana-hambana ka swihanyisi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: People Care: your family's needs come before market production
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: People Care: swilaveko swa ndyangu wa wena swi rhanga market production

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Fair Share: return surplus to the system — seeds, water, food, knowledge
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Ku Avelana hi Ku Ringana: vuyisela leswi saleke eka maendlelo ya nsimu — mbewu, mati, swakudya, vutivi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Ethics guide decisions when there's no rulebook
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Mahanyelo ma kongomisa swiboho loko ku nga ri na buku ya milawu

options.sourceEnglish: Keep all the borehole water for a larger irrigation area
options.xitsongaDraft: Hlayisa mati hinkwawo ya borehole ma tirhela ndhawu leyikulu ya ku cheleta ntsena

options.sourceEnglish: Find out if sharing is allowed and if the borehole can serve all users. Only then agree how to share fairly and keep watching the water level.
options.xitsongaDraft: Kuma leswaku xana ku avelana swa pfumeleriwa naswona borehole yi nga kota ku tirhela vatirhisi hinkwavo. Hi kona ntsena mi nga pfumelelanaka hi ndlela yo avelana hi ku ringana naswona mi ya emahlweni mi languta xiyimo xa mati.

options.sourceEnglish: Cap the borehole to preserve groundwater only
options.xitsongaDraft: Pfala borehole ku hlayisa mati ya le hansi ka misava ntsena

rationale.sourceEnglish: First find out what water use is allowed and whether the source can serve all users without taking too much. If sharing is allowed and there is enough water, agree how to share fairly. Monitoring helps you notice change; it does not give permission to take more water.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Rhanga u kuma leswaku hi kwihi ku tirhisiwa ka mati loku pfumeleriwaka na loko xihlovo xi nga kota ku tirhela vatirhisi hinkwavo handle ko teka mati yo tala ngopfu. Loko ku avelana ku pfumeleriwa naswona mati ma ringene, pfumelelanani hi ndlela yo avelana hi ku ringana. Ku xiyisisa swi ku pfuna ku vona ku cinca; a swi nyiki mpfumelelo wo teka mati yo tala.

title.xitsongaDraft: Misinya ya Milawu ya Khume-Mbirhi: Ku Endla Pulani na Ntumbuluko

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Twelve design principles arranged as segments around a central seedling, each shown as a simple picture — an eye for observing, a droplet for catching water, a sun for energy, a loop for returning waste.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Misinya ya milawu ya dizayini ya khume-mbirhi yi vekiwile hi swiphemu leswi rhendzeleke ximilana lexi nga exikarhini. Xiphemu xin’wana ni xin’wana xi kombisiwa hi xifaniso xo olova — tihlo ra ku xiyisisa, thonsi ra ku khoma mati, dyambu ra eneji, na xirhendzevutana lexi kombisaka ku vuyisa thyaka.

body.sourceEnglish:
David Holmgren set out twelve design principles in Essence of Permaculture. Bill Mollison and David Holmgren co-originated the permaculture concept. Three useful starting points for this lesson are: observe and interact — watch your land through a full season before major earthworks; catch and store energy — notice rain, sun and biomass before they leave your property; and use edges and value the marginal — a fence line or strip beside a path can be a useful place to observe.

Others worth knowing: produce no waste (scraps become compost, compost becomes soil), use small and slow solutions (a bucket can irrigate a bed without electricity), and use and value diversity. Hail injury to maize depends on the storm and the crop’s growth stage.

Pick two or three principles that speak to your biggest problem and apply them hard. The rest become obvious as you go.
body.xitsongaDraft:
David Holmgren u hlamuserile misinya ya milawu ya dizayini ya khume-mbirhi eka Essence of Permaculture. Bill Mollison na David Holmgren va sungule nongoti wa permaculture swin'we. Tindlela tinharhu to sungula leti pfunaka eka dyondzo leyi hi leti: observe and interact — languta ndhawu ya wena eka nguva leyi heleleke u nga si endla earthworks letikulu; catch and store energy — xiya mpfula, dyambu na biomass loko swi nga si suka eka ndhawu ya wena; na use edges and value the marginal — layini ya fence kumbe xiphemu xa misava lexi nga etlhelo ka ndlela (strip) xi nga va ndhawu leyi pfunaka ku xiyisisa.

Tin'wana leti faneleke ku tiviwa: produce no waste (masalela ma hundzuka compost, compost yi hundzuka misava), use small and slow solutions (bakiti ri nga cheleta planting bed handle ka gezi), na use and value diversity. Ku onhaka ka maize hi xihangu swi ya hi storm na growth stage ya xibyariwa.

Hlawula misinya ya milawu yimbirhi kumbe yinharhu leyi fambelanaka ni xiphiqo xa wena lexikulu, u yi tirhisa hi ku tiyimisela. Leyin'wana yi ta sungula ku vonaka loko u ri karhi u ya.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Observe your land for a full season before major earthworks
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Xiyisisa ndhawu ya wena eka nguva leyi heleleke u nga si sungula major earthworks

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Catch and store rain, sun, and biomass before they leave your property
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Hlengeleta u tlhela u hlayisa mpfula, dyambu na biomass swi nga si suka eka ndhawu ya wena

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Edges and margins can be useful places to observe what grows well
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Edges na margins swi nga va tindhawu leti pfunaka ku xiyisisa leswi kulaka kahle

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Hail injury to maize depends on the storm and the crop’s growth stage
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Ku onhaka ka maize hi xihangu swi ya hi storm na growth stage ya ximilana

question.sourceEnglish: A farmer wants to dig swales to harvest rainwater. What should she do first, following 'observe and interact'?
question.xitsongaDraft: Murimi u lava ku cela swales ku hlengeleta mati ya mpfula. I yini lexi a faneleke ku sungula hi xona, a landzela observe and interact?

options.sourceEnglish: Dig immediately after the first good rain
options.xitsongaDraft: Cela hi ku hatlisa endzhaku ka mpfula leyinene yo sungula

options.sourceEnglish: Watch where water flows and pools across at least one wet season
options.xitsongaDraft: Xiyisisa laha mati ma khulukaka kona ni laha ma hlengeletanaka kona eka nguva ya mpfula yin’we kumbe ku tlurisa

options.sourceEnglish: Copy a neighbour's swale layout
options.xitsongaDraft: Kopisa ndlela leyi swale ya muakelani yi endliweke ha yona

options.sourceEnglish: Assume the same swale design fits every site
options.xitsongaDraft: Anakanya leswaku design leyi fanaka ya swale ya faneleka eka ndhawu yin’wana ni yin’wana

rationale.sourceEnglish: A wet season shows more than one storm, but observation is only a first step. Check the soil, slope, drainage and safe overflow route with a trained local adviser before digging.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Nguva ya mpfula yi komba swidzedze swo tala ku tlula xin’we, kambe ku xiyisisa i goza ro sungula ntsena. Kambela misava, slope, drainage na safe overflow route swin’we na mutsundzuxi wa le ndhawini ya wena loyi a leteriweke u nga si cela.

question.sourceEnglish: Which layout best applies 'integrate rather than segregate'?
question.xitsongaDraft: Hi rihi hlelelo leri tirhisaka kahle integrate rather than segregate?

options.sourceEnglish: Chickens penned far from the garden
options.xitsongaDraft: Tihuku ti pfaleriwe ekule na ntanga

options.sourceEnglish: Garden, fruit trees and a chicken run arranged so chickens use an empty bed after harvest, then the farmer checks safe management before edible crops return
options.xitsongaDraft: Ntanga, mirhi ya mihandzu na chicken run swi hleriwe leswaku tihuku ti tirhisa planting bed leyi nga riki na swin'wana endzhaku ka harvest, kutani murimi u kambela safe management loko edible crops ti nga si vuya

options.sourceEnglish: Separate paddocks for each crop
options.xitsongaDraft: Paddocks to hambana eka crop yin’wana ni yin’wana

options.sourceEnglish: All animals kept off the cultivated zone
options.xitsongaDraft: Swiharhi hinkwaswo swi hlayisiwa swi nga ngheni eka cultivated zone

rationale.sourceEnglish: Integration puts each element to work for its neighbours — here, chickens clean up pests and add fertility instead of sitting idle in a fixed pen. Fresh manure can carry germs, so check safe management before edible crops return.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Ku hlanganisa swi endla leswaku element yin’wana ni yin’wana yi tirhela leswi nga ekusuhi na yona — laha, tihuku ti basisa pests ni ku engetela fertility, ematshan'weni yo tshamela eka fixed pen ti nga endli nto. Fresh manure yi nga rhwala germs, hikokwalaho kambela safe management loko edible crops ti nga si vuya.

title.sourceEnglish: Zones and Sectors: Organising Your Farm by Energy
title.xitsongaDraft: Ti-Zone na Ti-Sector: Ku Hlela Purasi ra Wena hi Matimba

infographicAlt.sourceEnglish: Illustrated example farm: numbered markers 0 to 5 follow a winding footpath from the house and near garden, past chickens and a field, toward trees and a wilder riverside area. The markers are examples, not fixed boundaries or distances.
infographicAlt.xitsongaDraft: Xikombiso xa purasi lexi kombisiweke hi swifaniso: tinomboro ta 0 ku ya eka 5 ti landzelela ndlela yo famba hi milenge leyi jikajikaka ku suka endlwini ni le xirhapeni xa le kusuhi, ti hundza tihuku ni nsimu, ti ya eka mirhi ni a wilder riverside area. Tinomboro leti i swikombiso ntsena; a hi mindzilakano leyi tiyisiweke kumbe mipfhuka leyi tiyisiweke.

body.sourceEnglish:
Zones and sectors help you cut wasted labour. Zones run 0 to 5 by how often you visit. Zone 0 is the house. In this example, Zone 1 is near the house and holds what you pick often — herbs, salad greens. Zone 2 is the main garden and chicken run, visited once or twice a day. Zone 3 is the main field, visited weekly. Zone 4 is semi-wild — fruit trees and fodder needing occasional attention. Zone 5 is left wild.

Sectors are the energies arriving from outside — sun, wind, rain, flood, fire. Watch where strong wind comes from on your farm. Nearby weather-station records can help you check wind direction. Watch where rainwater enters and flows across your land. Draw arrows for what you observe.

Sketch zones and sectors on paper and you have the skeleton of your design.
body.xitsongaDraft:
Zones na sectors swi ku pfuna ku hunguta ntirho lowu tlangisiwaka. Zones ti sukela eka 0 ku ya eka 5 hi ku ya hi ku tala ka minkarhi leyi u endzelaka ha yona. Zone 0 i yindlu. Eka example leyi, Zone 1 yi le kusuhi na yindlu naswona yi na leswi u swi tshovelaka nkarhi na nkarhi — herbs na salad greens. Zone 2 i ntanga lowukulu na xivala xa tihuku, leswi u swi endzelaka kan’we kumbe kambirhi hi siku. Zone 3 i nsimu leyikulu, leyi u yi endzelaka vhiki na vhiki. Zone 4 yi le ka semi-wild — mirhi ya mihandzu na fodder leyi lavaka nyingiso minkarhi yin’wana. Zone 5 yi tshikiwile yi ri nhova.

Sectors i energy leyi nghenaka yi huma ehandle — dyambu, moya, mpfula, flood na fire. Xiya laha moya lowu tiyeke wu humaka kona epurasini ra wena. Matsalwa ya weather station ya le kusuhi ma nga ku pfuna ku kambela tlhelo leri moya wu humaka eka rona. Xiya laha mati ya mpfula ma nghenaka kona ni laha ma khulukaka kona eka ndhawu ya wena. Dirowa miseve ya leswi u swi vonaka.

Dirowa zones na sectors ephepheni kutani u va na motheo wa design ya wena.

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: In this example, Zone 1 near the house holds often-picked herbs
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Eka example leyi, Zone 1 leyi nga kusuhi na yindlu yi na herbs leti u ti tshovelaka nkarhi na nkarhi

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Zones organise labour by how often you need to visit
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Ti-zone ti hlela mintirho hi ku ya hi minkarhi leyi u lavaka ku endzela ha yona

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: Sectors map incoming sun, wind, rainwater, flood and fire
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Sectors ti komba energy leyi nghenaka: dyambu, moya, mati ya mpfula, flood na ndzilo

keyPoints.sourceEnglish: A simple sketch of zones and sectors is enough to start designing
keyPoints.xitsongaDraft: Mpfapfarhuto wo olova wa ti-zone na ti-sector wu ringene ku sungula ku endla pulani

question.sourceEnglish: You plant herbs in Zone 3, the main field far from the house. What problem does this create?
question.xitsongaDraft: U byala herbs eka Zone 3, main field leyi nga ekule na yindlu. Xana leswi swi vanga xiphiqo xihi?

options.sourceEnglish: Herbs grow too large
options.xitsongaDraft: Herbs ti kula ngopfu

options.sourceEnglish: The extra walk may mean you pick or check them less often
options.xitsongaDraft: Ku famba mpfhuka wo engetela swi nga endla leswaku u tshovela kumbe u kambela herbs hi minkarhi yitsongo.

options.sourceEnglish: Herbs cross-pollinate with main crops
options.xitsongaDraft: Herbs ti cross-pollinate na crops letikulu

options.sourceEnglish: Zone 3 gets too much sun for herbs
options.xitsongaDraft: Zone 3 yi kuma sun yo tala ngopfu eka herbs

rationale.sourceEnglish: Put a crop you pick often near a daily path. A distant bed adds walking and may be checked less often.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Veka crop leyi u yi tshovelaka nkarhi na nkarhi ekusuhi na ndlela leyi u yi tirhisaka siku na siku. Bed leyi nga ekule yi engetela ku famba naswona yi nga endla leswaku u yi kambela hi minkarhi yitsongo.

question.sourceEnglish: You observe damaging wind coming from the north-west on a Highveld farm. Where should a windbreak go?
question.xitsongaDraft: U xiyisisa damaging wind coming from the North-west on a Highveld farm. Windbreak yi fanele ku ya kwihi?

options.sourceEnglish: South-east boundary
options.xitsongaDraft: Ndzilakana wa South-east

options.sourceEnglish: North-west boundary, between the wind and the crops
options.xitsongaDraft: Ndzilakana wa North-west, vhukati ka moya na crops

options.sourceEnglish: Centre of the property
options.xitsongaDraft: Exikari ka property

options.sourceEnglish: Windbreaks aren't needed since winds are seasonal
options.xitsongaDraft: Swisivela-moya a swi laveki hikuva mimoya yi hunga hi tinguva

rationale.sourceEnglish: A windbreak works by standing between the wind source and what it would damage — so it belongs on the side the wind actually comes from.
rationale.xitsongaDraft: Windbreak yi tirha hi ku yima vhukati ka laha moya wu humaka kona ni leswi wu nga swi onhaka. Hikokwalaho yi fanele ku va eka tlhelo leri moya wu humaka eka rona hakunene.
